speaker: N
text: It starts with a frying pan. Saturday, nine in the morning. You pick it up by the handle.

speaker: N
text: The metal handle. Straight off the flame.

speaker: N
text: Your sister stops chewing. You look down at your hand. The skin is going red. And you feel nothing.

speaker: MIA
text: Why aren't you screaming?

speaker: N
text: That's the question, isn't it. So, what if you couldn't feel pain?

speaker: N
text: Not less pain. None. No stings, no aches, no headaches, no hot handle. Ever again.

speaker: N
text: It sounds like a superpower. For about a week, it is.

speaker: N
text: Here's how it works. Rule one. Nothing hurts. Not a paper cut, not a broken arm, not a dentist's drill.

speaker: N
text: Rule two. You still get hurt. The burn still burns. The bone still breaks. You just don't get the message.

speaker: N
text: Rule three. Nobody can tell. You look fine. You always look fine. Remember that one.

speaker: N
text: And here's the strange part. This is real. There are people alive right now who were born this way.

speaker: N
text: In 2006, doctors in Cambridge studied families in Pakistan with a broken gene called SCN9A. One tiny switch inside the nerves, stuck off. None of them had ever felt pain.

speaker: N
text: One boy earned money in the street, walking on hot coals and pushing knives through his arms. He never felt a thing.

speaker: N
text: He died at fourteen. He jumped off a roof, because nothing had ever told him not to.

speaker: N
text: But you don't know any of that yet. You know you just held a hot pan for six seconds, and your Saturday has suddenly got very interesting.

speaker: N
text: So you test it. Like anyone would.

speaker: N
text: Test one. The hottest sauce in the shop. The one with the skull on the label. Theo cries from across the table.

speaker: THEO
text: Your face isn't even red. That's not normal, bro.

speaker: YOU
text: Tastes like ketchup.

speaker: N
text: Test two. The dentist. The one you've been avoiding for three years.

speaker: N
text: No injection. No gas. You watch the drill go in and think about lunch.

speaker: N
text: Test three. Five-a-side. The tackle that would have ended your season. You get up, pick the ball out of the net, and walk it back to the centre circle.

speaker: THEO
text: Bro. Your ankle is the wrong shape.

speaker: YOU
text: Feels fine.

speaker: N
text: And it does. That's the problem.

speaker: N
text: Plus. Headaches are gone. The gym stops being a punishment. You do a hundred press-ups, because nothing tells you to stop at thirty.

speaker: N
text: Minus. On Tuesday you bite your tongue at lunch, and you don't find out until Theo points at the blood.

speaker: N
text: Plus. You become a legend. The guy who can't feel. There's a video. It has four hundred thousand views.

speaker: N
text: Minus. The blister on your heel turns into a hole in your heel, because you walked on it for a week.

speaker: N
text: Here's the part the movies skip. Your body was never built for this. Pain is the only reason you ever moved your hand off a hot thing.

speaker: N
text: Touch a stove, and your spine yanks your arm back before your brain even knows. About a tenth of a second. It's a reflex, and it runs on the same alarm.

speaker: N
text: You just ripped the alarm out of the wall.

speaker: N
text: There's a woman in Scotland called Jo Cameron. Doctors found her in 2019. A different broken gene, the same result. She has never felt pain either.

speaker: N
text: She burns her arm on the oven and only notices when she smells it. So she checks her hands every night, the way you'd check a car for scratches.

speaker: N
text: Because when you can't feel the damage, you have to go looking for it.

speaker: N
text: And you? You stop looking. Why would you? You feel great.

speaker: N
text: Your grandad was a nurse for forty years. He watches you limp into the kitchen like nothing is wrong.

speaker: GRANDAD
text: Pain's not your enemy, son. Pain's the only friend who never lies to you.

speaker: YOU
text: Then I've got one less liar to worry about.

speaker: N
text: You'll remember that line. Just not yet.

speaker: N
text: Because here's what you build. A life with no warnings.

speaker: N
text: You skip the doctor. You sleep on your arm and wake up with a hand that doesn't work until noon. You eat food that's too hot, and your mouth becomes a map of burns you never felt.

speaker: N
text: Theo starts bringing a first-aid kit to football. Not for the team. For you.

speaker: N
text: And one Friday, around dinner, something in your stomach goes wrong. You don't know. You can't know.

speaker: N
text: You just notice you're not hungry. Then you notice you're cold. Then you notice nothing, because noticing was never your job. It was pain's job.

speaker: N
text: And here's where rule three comes back. Nobody can tell. You look fine.

speaker: N
text: Except one person. Theo. He's known you for eleven years. He looks at you across the table, and he doesn't see fine.

speaker: THEO
text: You've gone grey. You're sweating, and it's cold in here. When did you last eat?

speaker: YOU
text: I'm fine. Nothing hurts.

speaker: THEO
text: Yeah. That's what scares me.

speaker: N
text: Your appendix burst two hours ago. For anyone else, that's the worst pain of their life. For you, it's a Friday.

speaker: N
text: Theo drives. You tell him he's overreacting the whole way. At the hospital, a doctor with grey hair looks at the scan and goes very quiet.

speaker: DOCTOR
text: Most people walk in here screaming. You walked in because somebody looked at you. That somebody just saved your life.

speaker: N
text: Surgery takes an hour. Recovery takes three weeks. You feel none of it.

speaker: N
text: But you feel this. Lying there, you finally understand what your grandad meant.

speaker: N
text: Pain was never the enemy. Pain was the alarm. And when you can't hear the alarm, you need somebody watching for the smoke.

speaker: N
text: So you change. Not the power. You.

speaker: N
text: You check your hands every night, like Jo. You see a doctor every month, whether you like it or not. You let Theo look at you, and when he says you've gone grey, you believe him.

speaker: N
text: And at dinner, your sister pokes the scar on your stomach.

speaker: MIA
text: Did that hurt?

speaker: YOU
text: No.

speaker: MIA
text: Good. Then this won't.

speaker: N
text: And she punches your arm, as hard as a twelve-year-old can.

speaker: N
text: It doesn't hurt. But you laugh until it should.

speaker: N
text: Then your phone buzzes. Two in the morning. Theo.

speaker: N
text: "Mate. I just put my hand on the hob. And I didn't feel anything."

speaker: THEO
text: It's not just me.

speaker: YOU
text: How many?
